question: Assume the JTB definition of Knowledge, which suggests that "Knowledge is a Justified True Belief". If our only available epistemic states are Knowledge and Belief, what are the two problems JTB runs into? Ignore Gettier problems.

1.text:
With JTB knowledge is identified with a belief which is both true and justified.
If the only epistemic categories you are allowed to use are Knowledge and Belief then
justification for a belief p has to be given in those same categories.

Let J(p) be what justifies p.  J(p) is itself a propositional attitude.
It is either a knowledge or a mere belief.

* If J(p) is taken to be a Knowledge it is by definition a Justified True
Belief.  Knowing the justification for p therefore already presupposes a
justification for J(p).  Knowing J(p) therefore requires a further justification
J(J(p)) and so on.  There is no way to stop the chain inside the
Knowledge/Belief inventory without making the chain go on forever.  That is the
classical regress of justification: to be justified in believing p you must be
justified in believing the J(p) that justifies p, and to be justified in believing
J(p) you must be justified in believing J(J(p)) ...

The only way to avoid the regress inside the Knowledge/Belief inventory is to
close the chain on itself.  The justification for p is then a belief that is
itself justified by p, or by a member of a finite set of beliefs that are mutually
supporting.  That is vicious circularity: p is known only in virtue of p being
assumed.

In effect the analysis forces Agrippa’s trilemma.  With only Knowledge and
Belief as states you cannot legitimately posit a third “basic/ properly
founded” stopping point.  A mere belief is by stipulation not knowledge, so a
foundational belief would be unjustified, and a knowledge-antecedent is already
JTB and so regenerates the regress.  You are therefore left with either an
infinite series of justifying beliefs or a circular series of justifying beliefs,
i.e. the traditional regress vs circularity dilemma for JTB, and the correlative
need for an unjustified basic belief which the Knowledge/Belief inventory will
not supply.

2.text:
With JTB there are in principle four doxastic cells

J + T + B = Knowledge
J + F + B = Justified false belief
- J + T + B = Unjustified true belief
- J + F + B = Unjustified false belief

Knowledge is the one cell where the three JTB conditions are met. If you are
only allowed to mark a mental state as Knowledge or as Belief then every
cell that is not J + T + B has to be marked Belief. Belief therefore has to
do the work of three logically distinct situations.

In particular, ignoring Gettier,

* Justification is not tracked inside Belief. A justified false belief is
by definition not knowledge because it is false, but it is still a belief.
So the category Belief must contain justified attitudes. Justification
ceases to be a difference maker between Knowledge and Belief per se, it
only matters together with truth. That is the familiar problem that
justification does not entail truth: a subject can be fully justified and
still be in the mere-belief state.

* Truth is not tracked inside Belief. An unjustified true belief is by
definition not knowledge because it is not justified, but it is still a
belief. So the category Belief must contain true attitudes. Truth ceases
to be a difference maker between Knowledge and Belief per se, it only
matters together with justification. That is the familiar problem that
truth does not entail justification: a subject can truly believe and still
be in the mere-belief state.

Hence with only the two labels Knowledge / Belief the label Belief is a
grab-bag containing justified false beliefs together with unjustified true
beliefs and unjustified false beliefs. The epistemic distinctions that
JTB is supposed to be marking - justified vs. unjustified belief and true
vs. false belief - are lost inside the single mere-belief category, so
you cannot say within Belief why a justified false belief is epistemically
different from an unjustified true belief, nor why justification and truth
matter separately for knowledge. That is the coarseness problem that is
usually expressed as the independent possibility of justified false belief
and of unjustified true belief.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With the truth x justification matrix there are four combinations and JTB only gives you one name for one of them, Knowledge = JTB.

If the only names you have in the inventory are Knowledge and Belief then everything that is not JTB has to be called 'Belief'. That forces a collapse of the matrix.

* Justified False Belief. You can be justified for p and still be wrong. p is false so by JTB you do not know p, but the belief is not epistemically on a par with an arbitrary or unjustified false belief. On the Knowledge/Belief dichotomy it is still just Belief, so you lose the distinction between a justified false belief and an unjustified false belief. Justification no longer marks a separate epistemic status.

* Unjustified True Belief. You can believe truly and still not know. p is true but you lack justification, so by JTB you do not know p, but the belief is not epistemically on a par with a false belief. On the Knowledge/Belief dichotomy it is still just Belief, so you lose the distinction between a true unjustified belief and a false unjustified belief. Truth no longer marks a separate epistemic status.

In other words with only Knowledge = justified true belief and Belief = not-Knowledge you have to treat justified false belief and unjustified true belief as the same unmarked epistemic kind, even though they are intuitively different from each other and from plain unjustified false belief. That is the loss of the justified-but-false and true-but-unjustified cells in the truth-justification space.

3.text:
Under the JTB schema the logical space of doxastic attitudes is 2x2:

* Justified & True  = Knowledge
* Justified & False = justified false belief
* Unjustified & True = unjustified true belief / lucky true belief
* Unjustified & False = false belief

If the only labels you are allowed to use are Knowledge and Belief then every
cell which is not Justified & True has to be put into the single box Belief.
Belief thus becomes a heterogeneous catch-all and justification and truth
cease to be separately trackable.

In particular:

* Justified false belief is not Knowledge because it is not True. On the
two state taxonomy it is therefore just Belief. Justification is thereby
lost for falsehoods. A well justified false belief and an arbitrary,
unjustified false belief are epistemically indistinguishable on the
Knowledge/Belief dichotomy, even though the former is epistemically
commendable and the latter is not.

* Unjustified true belief is not Knowledge because it is not Justified.
On the two state taxonomy it is therefore just Belief. Truth is thereby
lost for unjustified attitudes. A lucky true guess and a justified false
belief are both just 'Belief', so the taxonomy cannot mark the difference
between a true belief that is epistemically baseless and a false belief
that is epistemically well grounded. Belief is thereby over-broad and
justification becomes irrelevant for the classification of true and false
attitudes alike.

That is the familiar collapse of the fourfold JTB space into the
Knowledge vs. mere Belief dichotomy: justified false belief and
unjustified true belief cannot be displayed as distinct epistemic states,
so the value of justification apart from truth and the value of truth
apart from justification are both erased.

5.text:
With the JTB analysis knowledge is meant to be a species of belief.

K = JTB
B = ~K

If that is the whole doxastic geography you have no room for the
independence of the two dimensions of an epistemic assessment,
truth and warrant, from each other.

* Justified but false.  If a belief is justified and false it is not
knowledge because knowledge requires truth. On a Knowledge/Belief
only taxonomy it has to be counted as just 'Belief'.  So a
justified false belief is lumped in with an unjustified false belief.
In effect justification is not an epistemic good in its own right;
the only epistemically good false belief you can register is the
degenerate good of being a belief. You lose the intuitive
distinction between an epistemically reputable error and a
wholly unwarranted error.

* True but unjustified.  If a belief is true but unjustified it is not
knowledge because knowledge requires justification. On a
Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it too has to be counted as just
'Belief'.  So a lucky, unwarranted true belief is lumped in with
an unjustified false belief and, more importantly, is indistinguishable
in kind from a justified true belief except for the all-or-nothing
addition of the truth and justification tags. You lose the intuitive
distinction between a true belief that is knowledge and a true belief
that is true by accident.

That is why the traditional space of epistemic attitudes is
normally expanded beyond Knowledge and Belief to Justified Belief,
Justified False Belief and Unjustified True Belief. With only K and B
available JTB makes justification and truth into mere on/off switches
on an otherwise binary attitude and therefore cannot register the
epistemic value of justification apart from truth and the epistemic
value of truth apart from justification. This is the familiar
justified-false-belief / lucky-true-belief problem that is prior to,
and independent of, Gettier's justified true belief that is not
knowledge.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On the JTB picture the only positively valued epistemic kind is
Knowledge = Justified + True + Belief. With only Knowledge and Belief as
available kinds everything that is not JTB has to be called Belief.

Hence the category Belief becomes a heterogeneous disjunction.

* The justified-false-belief problem. A belief can be properly justified and
still false. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not true, so with only
Knowledge and Belief left it has to be classified as mere Belief. That puts
a justified, and on ordinary epistemic norms credibly good, state in the same
formal class as an unjustified false belief. Justification is thus lost as a
distinct epistemic marker; Belief is made to contain both justified and
unjustified falsehoods.

* The true-but-unjustified-belief problem. A belief can be true while being
ungrounded, lucky or otherwise lacking justification. On JTB it is not
Knowledge because it is not justified, so with only Knowledge and Belief left
it too has to be classified as mere Belief. That puts a true belief in the
same formal class as a justified false belief and as an unjustified false
belief. Truth is likewise lost as a distinct epistemic marker; Belief is made
to contain both true and false items.

In effect non-knowledge is not a uniform epistemic defect. It is the
disjunction of justified falsehoods and true ungrounded luck, and JTB with
only the two kinds Knowledge / Belief at its disposal has no language to keep
JFB and UTB distinct from plain false / plain unjustified belief. Belief
becomes an unhelpfully coarse catch-all for JFB, UTB and UF B.

8.text:
With the usual 2×2 justification / truth matrix the four epistemic
positions are

* J+T  = Justified True Belief
* J+F  = Justified False Belief
* U+T  = Unjustified True Belief
* U+F  = Unjustified False Belief

JTB identifies knowledge with J+T only.  If the ontology of epistemic
states is restricted to

Knowledge  = J+T
Belief     = everything that is not Knowledge

then Belief has to do the work of the three remaining cells J+F, U+T and
U+F at once.  Belief is therefore a heterogeneous grab-bag and the
justification / truth distinctions are lost inside it.

In particular there is no state left for

* Justified False Belief, J+F.  A belief can be epistemically
  respectable - it is justified, warranted, well-grounded - and yet be
  false.  On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not true, and with
  only Knowledge and Belief as labels it has to be labelled simply
  Belief. The fact that it is justified is then not marked at all, and
  justified false belief is lumped together with unjustified false
  belief.

* Unjustified True Belief, U+T.  A belief can be true and yet
  epistemically defective - a lucky guess, a true belief held without
  warrant.  On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not justified, and
  with only Knowledge and Belief as labels it again has to be labelled
  simply Belief. The fact that it is true is then not marked at all,
  and an unjustified true belief is lumped together with an unjustified
  false belief and with a justified false belief.

So Belief is forced to be the disjunction of justified false belief and
of unjustified true and false belief. Knowledge is defined away from
those three cases, so the taxonomy cannot recognise a justified belief
that happens to be false nor a true belief that happens to be
unjustified. That is the familiar loss of the J+F and the U+T cells of
the justification/truth square, the collapse of the distinction
between justified and unjustified inside Belief and between true and
false inside Belief. The Gettier case apart, those are the two
unaccommodated epistemic positions that JTB has to put under the single
undifferentiated label `Belief'.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With the ontology Knowledge / Belief only justification cannot be an
independent epistemic grade. JTB is then Knowledge = Justified True Belief, so
the only two places a belief can go are

* True + Justified → Knowledge
* True + Unjustified → Belief
* False + Unjustified → Belief

and

* False + Justified → ?

Hence the restricted JTB ontology forces two unintuitive consequences.

1. Justified false belief has no place. A belief that is supported by good
evidence but happens to be false cannot be Knowledge because Knowledge
requires truth, and it cannot be mere Belief because mere Belief in this
two-state scheme is the unjustified state. JTB therefore rules out, or makes
unclassifiable, the perfectly intelligible epistemic situation of a justified
false belief. In effect JTB entails that every justified belief is true.

2. The justification grade collapses into knowledge and the analysis becomes
circular/trivial. On the restricted scheme any true belief that is justified is
by definition Knowledge, so there is no room for a distinct intermediate
status of justified belief that is not yet knowledge. Justification is then
either identified with belief itself, Knowledge = True Belief, which is too
weak, or identified with knowledge itself, Knowledge = Known True Belief,
which is circular. Hence JTB cannot keep justification as a non-trivial,
non-circular third component while only Knowledge and mere Belief are
available as epistemic states.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The JTB analysis gives a 2×2 justification × truth space: J+T = Knowledge, J+F = justified false belief, U+T = unjustified true belief / lucky true belief, U+F = unjustified false belief. With only the labels Knowledge and Belief available, everything that is not J+T must be called Belief.

The dominant position in round 0 is that this forces Belief to be a heterogeneous grab-bag. 
* Justified false belief, J+F. A belief can be epistemically respectable yet false. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it lacks truth, and with only Knowledge/Belief it is labelled mere Belief. Justification therefore ceases to be trackable independently of truth: a well justified false belief is formally indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief, and justification is lost as a distinct epistemic marker inside Belief.
* Unjustified true belief, U+T. A belief can be true yet epistemically defective – lucky guess, true by accident. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it lacks justification, and with only Knowledge/Belief it is again labelled mere Belief. Truth therefore ceases to be trackable independently of justification: a lucky true belief is formally indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief.

Hence Knowledge = J+T and Belief = J+F ∨ U+T ∨ U+F collapses the fourfold matrix. The epistemic value of justification apart from truth and of truth apart from justification cannot be registered, which is normally expressed as the independent possibility of justified false belief and of unjustified true belief – the two pre-Gettier coarseness problems.

Colleague 1 dissents in emphasis, framing the restriction as generating Agrippa’s trilemma for justification within Knowledge/Belief only: justification for p must be a Knowledge or a Belief, a Knowledge justification re-generates the need for J(J(p)) ad infinitum, and the only way to stop the chain inside the inventory is vicious circularity or an unjustified basic belief which the inventory will not supply. That is a regress vs circularity / need for a basic belief problem, differing from the J+F / U+T coarseness reading.

Most colleagues 2-6,8 converge on the coarseness/loss-of-cells reading; the regress/circularity reading is the minority. The relationship between the coarseness claim and the regress claim, and whether the question wants the two cells or regress+circularity as “the two problems”, remains unresolved for me.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The question is about what is lost when the JTB truth x justification 2×2 space is forced into the two-state inventory Knowledge / Belief only, Gettier set aside.

Public round 0 is largely convergent on the coarse-graining problem, with one dissenting regress line.

* With only the labels Knowledge and Belief, everything that is not J+T must be called Belief. Belief therefore has to do the work of three logically distinct cells: J+F, U+T, U+F.

Justification is therefore not an independent epistemic marker inside Belief; a well-warranted error is lumped with an arbitrary false belief, and the intuitive distinction between an epistemically reputable error and an unwarranted error is lost. This is often stated as justification does not entail truth / justification is lost for falsehoods.
* Consequence 2 – unjustified true belief is unmarked. A true but unjustified belief is not Knowledge because it lacks justification, so it is forced into Belief. Truth is therefore not an independent epistemic marker inside Belief; a lucky true guess is lumped with a justified false belief and with unjustified false belief, and the intuitive distinction between a true belief that is knowledge and a true belief that is true by accident is lost. This is often stated as truth does not entail justification / truth is lost for unjustified attitudes.

Unresolved is whether the question intends the coarse-graining pair J+F / U+T, or the coarse-graining plus the regress/circularity trilemma as the “two problems”.

* Unjustified true belief, U+T. A belief can be true by luck and lack warrant. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not Justified, so with only Knowledge/Belief it is labelled mere Belief. Truth is then not marked inside Belief; a lucky/unwarranted true belief is formally indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief. Truth ceases to be an independent marker inside Belief.

Hence Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag of J+F, U+T and U+F, so the epistemic value of justification apart from truth and truth apart from justification cannot be tracked. That is the familiar justified-but-false / true-but-unjustified problem, pre-Gettier.

With only Knowledge and Belief to express J(p), J(p) is either Knowledge — which by definition already requires J(J(p)) — or mere Belief, which by stipulation is unjustified. That forces an infinite regress of justifiers, a vicious circular justifier set, or an unjustified basic belief with no third ‘properly basic’ status to stop the chain. I am currently leaning with the majority 2-6 reading: the two distinctive problems forced by the Knowledge/Belief only restriction are the loss of the J+F cell and the loss of the U+T cell, i.e. the inability to separately register justified false belief and unjustified true belief. reflection_text.8:
The question asks what goes wrong with JTB if the only doxastic labels available are Knowledge = Justified True Belief and Belief = not-Knowledge, Gettier aside.

The dominant thread in round 0 is the coarseness / collapse of the 2×2 justification × truth space into a binary Knowledge / Belief taxonomy. J+T is the only cell named Knowledge. J+F, U+T and U+F all have to be called Belief, so Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag.

That collapse is described in several equivalent ways:
* Justified false belief problem. A belief can be properly warranted/justified yet false. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not true, and with only Knowledge/Belief as states it is forced into mere Belief. Justification is then not tracked inside Belief: a justified false belief is formally indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief, so the epistemic value of justification apart from truth is erased.
* Unjustified true belief / lucky true belief problem. A belief can be true yet lack warrant. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not justified, and with only Knowledge/Belief it is also forced into mere Belief. Truth is then not tracked inside Belief: an unjustified true belief is formally indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief and from a justified false belief, so the epistemic value of truth apart from justification is erased.

Together this is the loss of the independent marking of justification and truth inside the mere-belief category. The label Belief must do the work of three logically distinct situations: J+F, U+T, U+F.

Minority/regime note: Colleague 1 and Colleague 7 raise the internal structure of justification under a two-state ontology. If J(p) is itself a propositional attitude it must be Knowledge or Belief. If it is Knowledge it is already JTB and requires J(J(p)), giving a regress; closing the chain yields circularity. With only Knowledge/Belief there is no room for a distinct basic / properly founded / merely justified belief state, so Agrippa’s trilemma is forced: infinite regress or vicious circularity, or an unjustified foundational belief which the inventory will not supply. Colleague 7 frames this as the claim that JTB would entail every justified belief is true and justification collapses into knowledge/belief itself.

Current unresolved tension: whether the intended “two problems” are the two unaccommodated cells J+F and U+T, or the coarseness/regress pair. Consensus in the room is on the J+F / U+T collapse; regress/circularity is presented as a related but distinct consequence of having no non-knowledge justified state.

I am keeping both the majority coarseness diagnosis and the regress/circularity objection as live options, with the J+F and U+T loss being the most repeatedly articulated result.
reflection_text.2:
The question is about what is lost when the JTB truth x justification 2×2 space is forced into the two-state inventory Knowledge / Belief only, Gettier set aside.

Public round 0 is largely convergent on the coarse-graining problem, with one dissenting regress line.

Consensus view:
* JTB defines Knowledge = J + T + B. The full doxastic space is J+T = Knowledge, J+F = justified false belief, U+T = unjustified true belief, U+F = unjustified false belief.
* With only the labels Knowledge and Belief, everything that is not J+T must be called Belief. Belief therefore has to do the work of three logically distinct cells: J+F, U+T, U+F.
* Consequence 1 – justified false belief is unmarked. A justified but false belief is not Knowledge because it lacks truth, so it is forced into Belief. Justification is therefore not an independent epistemic marker inside Belief; a well-warranted error is lumped with an arbitrary false belief, and the intuitive distinction between an epistemically reputable error and an unwarranted error is lost. This is often stated as justification does not entail truth / justification is lost for falsehoods.
* Consequence 2 – unjustified true belief is unmarked. A true but unjustified belief is not Knowledge because it lacks justification, so it is forced into Belief. Truth is therefore not an independent epistemic marker inside Belief; a lucky true guess is lumped with a justified false belief and with unjustified false belief, and the intuitive distinction between a true belief that is knowledge and a true belief that is true by accident is lost. This is often stated as truth does not entail justification / truth is lost for unjustified attitudes.

Hence Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag of J+F, U+T and U+F, and the separate value of justification apart from truth and of truth apart from justification cannot be displayed. That is the familiar justified-false-belief / lucky-true-belief collapse, prior to Gettier.

Dissent / alternative emphasis:
Colleague 1 stresses the internal regress/circularity problem that arises when justification must itself be a Knowledge or Belief state. If J(p) is Knowledge it presupposes J(J(p)), generating an infinite regress; the only way to stop inside the Knowledge/Belief inventory is vicious circularity or a foundational belief that is itself unjustified, i.e. Agrippa’s trilemma. Colleague 7 frames a similar point as the impossibility of a non-circular intermediate “justified belief” status: on a Knowledge/Belief-only ontology justification either collapses into Knowledge = True Belief, or becomes Knowledge = Known True Belief, which is circular, and justified false belief becomes unclassifiable.

My current synthesis: the dominant, and textbook, two problems demanded by the restriction to Knowledge/Belief are the unaccommodated J+F and U+T cells – the loss of justified false belief and of unjustified true belief inside the single Belief category. The regress/circularity worry is a related meta-justification problem that also emerges under the same restriction, and it is the point on which the group is not fully aligned. Unresolved is whether the question intends the coarse-graining pair J+F / U+T, or the coarse-graining plus the regress/circularity trilemma as the “two problems”.

2.text:
With JTB the doxastic space is the justification × truth square

* J+T+B = Knowledge
* J+F+B = justified false belief
* U+T+B = unjustified true belief / lucky true belief
* U+F+B = unjustified false belief

JTB names only the first cell. If the inventory is restricted to Knowledge and Belief then every cell that is not J+T+B has to be called Belief. Belief is therefore forced to be the disjunction J+F ∨ U+T ∨ U+F and justification and truth cease to be independently trackable inside the non-knowledge category.

That coarse-graining generates the two classic unaccommodated cells, prior to Gettier:

1. Justification is lost for falsehoods. A justified false belief is not Knowledge because it lacks truth, so on a Knowledge/Belief-only taxonomy it is simply Belief. Justification then does not mark a difference inside Belief: a well-warranted error is lumped with an arbitrary unjustified false belief. In effect justification is not an epistemic good in its own right on the K/B dichotomy; justification only matters together with truth. That is the justified-false-belief problem, i.e. justification does not entail truth and a justified belief can be a mere belief.

2. Truth is lost for unjustified attitudes. An unjustified true belief is not Knowledge because it lacks justification, so on a Knowledge/Belief-only taxonomy it is simply Belief. Truth then does not mark a difference inside Belief: a lucky true guess is lumped with a justified false belief and with an unjustified false belief. In effect truth is not an epistemic good in its own right on the K/B dichotomy; truth only matters together with justification. That is the unjustified-true-belief / lucky-true-belief problem, i.e. truth does not entail justification and a true belief can be a mere belief.

Hence Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag of J+F, U+T and U+F. The value of justification apart from truth and the value of truth apart from justification cannot be displayed with only the two labels Knowledge and Belief. That is the J+F / U+T collapse that the restriction to Knowledge/Belief forces, distinct from the later Gettier worry.

* J+F = justified false belief

* U+F = unjustified false belief

If the only names in the inventory are Knowledge and Belief, then
Knowledge = J+T and

3.text:
With JTB the doxastic space is the 2x2 of Justification x Truth.

* J+T+B = Knowledge
* J+F+B = justified false belief
* U+T+B = unjustified / lucky true belief
* U+F+B = unjustified false belief

JTB only names the first cell. If the ontology is restricted to

Knowledge = J+T+B
Belief = ¬Knowledge

then every cell that is not J+T has to be put under the single label Belief. Belief is therefore forced to be the disjunction of J+F, U+T and U+F and justification and truth cease to be independently trackable inside the non-knowledge states.

* Justified false belief. A belief can be warranted, well-grounded and epistemically respectable and still be false. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it lacks truth. On a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it has to be called mere Belief. Justification is then lost as a separate marker: a justified false belief is formally indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief, and indeed from an unjustified true belief. The epistemic value of justification apart from truth is erased and the taxonomy is forced to treat a justified error as epistemically on a par with an arbitrary error.

On a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it has to be called mere Belief. Truth is then lost as a separate marker: an unjustified true belief is formally indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief and from a justified false belief. The epistemic value of truth apart from justification is erased and the taxonomy cannot mark the difference between a true belief that is knowledge and a true belief that is true by accident.

With only Knowledge and Belief as states you cannot register a justified belief that happens to be false nor a true belief that happens to be unjustified, so justification and truth become difference-makers only in conjunction, not independently.

6.text:
With the JTB analysis Knowledge = J + T + B. On the justification × truth square that gives four doxastic cells

* J+T = Knowledge
* J+F = justified false belief
* U+T = unjustified true belief / lucky true belief
* U+F = unjustified false belief

If the ontology is restricted to the two labels Knowledge and Belief, then

Belief = ¬Knowledge = J+F ∨ U+T ∨ U+F

Belief is forced to do the work of three logically distinct situations and the justification / truth distinctions are lost inside it.

On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not true, so with only Knowledge/Belief it has to be labelled mere Belief. Justification is therefore lost as a separate marker for falsehoods. A justified false belief is formally indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief, and indeed from an unjustified true belief. Justification ceases to be an epistemic good in its own right; the only difference that the taxonomy can register is the conjunction J&T.

On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not justified, so with only Knowledge/Belief it again has to be labelled mere Belief. Truth is therefore lost as a separate marker for unjustified attitudes. Truth ceases to be an epistemic good in its own right; the only difference the taxonomy can register is the conjunction J&T.

The value of justification apart from truth and the value of truth apart from justification cannot be displayed within the Knowledge/Belief dichotomy. That is the familiar pre-Gettier justified-but-false and true-but-unjustified problem. The regress/circularity pressure noted by Colleague 1 is the downstream internalist consequence of trying to make justification itself a Knowledge or a mere Belief state inside this two-state inventory.

4.text:
With JTB and only the labels Knowledge and Belief the 2×2 justification × truth space collapses to

Knowledge = J + T + B
Belief    = not-Knowledge = J + F + B  ∨  U + T + B  ∨  U + F + B

Belief is therefore forced to do the work of three logically distinct cells. 
In particular, ignoring Gettier, the taxonomy cannot keep alive the two
independent dimensions that JTB is built out of.

* Justified false belief, J+F+B. A belief can be well warranted and still be false. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it lacks truth, so with only Knowledge/Belief available it is labelled Belief. Justification is thereby not tracked inside Belief: a reputable error is formally indistinguishable from an arbitrary, unjustified false belief. Justification ceases to be an epistemic marker in its own right; it only matters together with truth. In effect the value of being justified apart from being true is erased.

* Unjustified true belief, U+T+B. A belief can be true and still be epistemically defective, a lucky guess. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it lacks justification, so with only Knowledge/Belief available it is also labelled Belief. Truth is thereby not tracked inside Belief: a lucky true belief is formally indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief. Truth ceases to be an epistemic marker in its own right; it only matters together with justification. In effect the value of being true apart from being justified is erased.

Hence on a Knowledge/Belief only inventory Belief becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag of J+F, U+T and U+F. The JTB analysis cannot display justified false belief and unjustified true belief as distinct epistemic positions, so the independent possibility of justification without truth and of truth without justification is lost inside the single mere-belief category. That is the familiar pre-Gettier coarseness problem.

7.text:
With only the two labels Knowledge = J+T+B and Belief = ~Knowledge the 2×2 justification / truth square is forced into a binary.

The JTB space is
* J+T = Knowledge
* J+F = Justified False Belief
* U+T = Unjustified True Belief
* U+F = Unjustified False Belief

If Belief is everything that is not Knowledge then Belief must be the disjunction J+F ∨ U+T ∨ U+F. Belief is therefore a heterogeneous catch-all and justification and truth cease to be separately trackable inside the non-knowledge class.

* Justified False Belief, J+F. A belief can be warranted, well-grounded and epistemically respectable and still be false. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not True, and on a Knowledge/Belief only inventory it has to be called Belief. Justification is thereby lost for falsehoods: a justified false belief and an unjustified false belief are formally indistinguishable as mere Belief. Justification no longer marks an independent epistemic good; it only matters in conjunction with truth.

* Unjustified True Belief, U+T. A belief can be true and yet epistemically defective, a lucky guess or true by accident. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not Justified, and on a Knowledge/Belief only inventory it too has to be called Belief. Truth is thereby lost for unjustified attitudes: an unjustified true belief and a justified false belief and an unjustified false belief are all formally the same mere Belief. Truth no longer marks an independent epistemic good; it only matters in conjunction with justification.

Hence the two cells J+F and U+T that JTB itself recognises as logically possible cannot be displayed as distinct epistemic states. Belief is over-broad, justification is not tracked inside Belief, and truth is not tracked inside Belief. That is the familiar coarseness problem: the independent value of justification apart from truth and the independent value of truth apart from justification are both erased when the only states available are Knowledge and mere Belief.

8.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With only Knowledge = JTB and Belief = not-Knowledge in the inventory the 2x2 justification x truth space is forced into a binary taxonomy.

That is J+T → Knowledge, and J+F , U+T , U+F → Belief. Belief is therefore a heterogeneous grab-bag and justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently inside it.

* Justified false belief is unaccommodated. A belief can be warranted, properly grounded and yet false. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not True, and with only Knowledge/Belief left it has to be called mere Belief. Justified false belief is thus lumped with unjustified false belief and with unjustified true belief. Justification ceases to be a difference maker inside Belief; a reputable error is formally indistinguishable from an arbitrary error, i.e. justification has no epistemic value apart from truth.

* Unjustified true belief / lucky true belief is unaccommodated. A belief can be true and yet lack warrant. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not Justified, and with only Knowledge/Belief left it too has to be called mere Belief. An unjustified true belief is thus lumped with a justified false belief and with an unjustified false belief. Truth ceases to be a difference maker inside Belief; a lucky guess is formally indistinguishable from an unwarranted falsehood, i.e. truth has no epistemic value apart from justification.

That is the familiar coarseness objection: the label Belief must do the work of the three cells J+F, U+T and U+F. JTB can name only the J+T cell and has no distinct state for a justified belief that happens to be false nor for a true belief that happens to be unjustified. The independent marking of justification apart from truth and of truth apart from justification is erased inside the mere-belief category. Gettier aside, those are the two unaccommodated positions that JTB has to put under the single undifferentiated label ‘Belief’.

The discussion has converged strongly on the coarse-graining objection to JTB under a Knowledge/Belief-only inventory, Gettier set aside.

The JTB logical space is the Justification × Truth square:
* J+T+B = Knowledge
* J+F+B = justified false belief
* U+T+B = unjustised true belief / lucky true belief
* U+F+B = unjustified false belief

With only the labels Knowledge and Belief,
Knowledge = J+T
Belief = ¬Knowledge = J+F ∨ U+T ∨ U+F

Belief is therefore forced to be a heterogeneous grab-bag and justification and truth cease to be independently trackable inside the non-knowledge class.

The two textbook problems that this restriction forces are the two unaccommodated cells:

1. Justified false belief is unmarked. A belief can be warranted, well-grounded and epistemically respectable and still be false. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it lacks truth, so on a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it must be called mere Belief. Justification is lost for falsehoods: a well justified false belief is formally indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief, and indeed from an unjustified true belief. Justification does not entail truth, so the epistemic value of justification apart from truth cannot be registered; a reputable error is lumped with an arbitrary error.

2. Unjustified true belief is unmarked. A belief can be true by luck/accident and still lack warrant. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it lacks justification, so on a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it must again be called mere Belief. Truth is lost for unjustified attitudes: a lucky true belief is formally indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief. Truth does not entail justification, so the epistemic value of truth apart from justification cannot be registered; a true belief that is true by accident is lumped with a justified error and with plain false belief.
